Working in the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma). I'm planning a large expansion of Nxeon's existing internal Discord integration into a full public+staff hybrid Discord server. I need a thorough, accurate map of everything that already exists so the plan reuses it correctly instead of duplicating it.

Please read FULLY (not just excerpts) and report back:

1. `lib/discord.ts` — every exported function and its exact signature (e.g. discordEnabled, discordBotToken, discordApplicationId, discordGuildId, discordPublicKey, verifyDiscordSignature, createGuildTextChannel, postChannelMessage, any REST helper, InteractionType enum values, replyModalResponse, channelMessageResponse, extractModalText, extractInteractionUserId, getDiscordUserById). Note the base URL and auth header pattern used for Discord REST calls, and whether there's a generic "make an authenticated Discord REST request" helper I could reuse for creating channels/roles/permission-overwrites.

2. `lib/discord-bridge.ts` — full read. Exactly how does the ticket/chat "mirror to a private text channel" work today (channel creation, naming, permission overwrites if any, message mirroring both directions)? How does `resolveDiscordReplyActor` work? Is there anything today that already restricts a channel to specific Discord users/roles (permission overwrites), or is every mirrored channel visible to the whole guild currently?

3. `lib/discord-status-alerts.ts` — full read, exact functions (alertIncidentOpened/Resolved/Reopened) and how they're triggered.

4. `lib/discord-oauth.ts` and `lib/actions-discord-link.ts` — full read. Exact OAuth flow (authorize URL construction, scopes requested, callback handling, where `User.discordUserId` gets written), and the exact gating (`requireArea("support")`) that currently limits this to staff only. Also check `app/api/admin/discord/authorize/route.ts` and `app/api/admin/discord/callback/route.ts`.

5. `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts` — full read, exact interaction-type handling (PING, MESSAGE_COMPONENT, MODAL_SUBMIT) and confirm APPLICATION_COMMAND (slash commands) is indeed unhandled today.

6. Search the whole codebase for every place `discordUserId`, `discordThreadId`, `discordGuildId`, `discord_enabled`, `discord_guild_id`, `discord_status_alerts_channel_id` are read or written, to catch any other integration point I might have missed (e.g. is there an admin settings UI page for these values — find its file path).

7. Check `prisma/schema.prisma` for the exact `User`, `Ticket`, `ChatConversation` model fields relevant to Discord, plus their relations to `Server`/`Plan`/`Role` (I need to know what "plan tier" data is queryable off a User for role-assignment purposes — e.g. does User have a direct plan/tier field, or is it derived from their active Server/HostingAccount/GameServer rows? What Role enum values exist today, e.g. CUSTOMER/SUPPORT/BILLING/ADMIN?).

Report back with concrete file:line references and exact function signatures/names — I'll be writing a real implementation plan from your findings, so precision matters more than a narrative summary. Do not propose new code or a plan yourself — this is pure fact-finding.

1	// Typed access layer over the key/value `Setting` store (db.setting).
2	//
3	// Plain (non-"use server") module so it can export the SETTINGS_DEFAULTS map,
4	// types and pure helpers alongside the async DB getters/setters. Import it from
5	// server components, server actions and the worker. Do NOT import from client
6	// components.
7	//
8	// Every admin-editable knob lives here with a default, so reads are total: a key
9	// that has never been written falls back to its SETTINGS_DEFAULTS value. Booleans
10	// are stored as the strings "true"/"false"; money is stored in cents; percents as
11	// plain numbers (e.g. "8.5" = 8.5%).
12	
13	import { db } from "./db";
14	import { VPS_TERMS } from "./billing-terms";
15	
16	export const SETTINGS_DEFAULTS = {
17	  // --- General / Branding ---
18	  //
19	  // Every default in this block is the string that was previously HARDCODED at the
20	  // render site it now feeds. That matters: `getSetting` falls back to these, so a
21	  // platform with an empty `Setting` table must render exactly what it rendered
22	  // before the wiring landed. A default of "" here would have blanked the footer
23	  // tagline and produced an empty `mailto:` on /contact the moment these keys were
24	  // read for the first time.
25	  brand_name: "Nxeon",
26	  // Verbatim the copy that used to be inline in components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx.
27	  // The footer is this key's only consumer, so the panel now previews what actually ships.
28	  brand_tagline:
29	    "Premium NVMe cloud VPS hosting, provisioned in seconds. Built for developers, teams, and everything you ship.",
30	  // Was "". The contact page advertises this address in three places and every one of
31	  // them hardcoded it, so the panel showed a blank support email while the marketing
32	  // site published a real one — and reading the blank key would have shipped
33	  // `mailto:` with no recipient.
34	  support_email: "support@nxeon.cloud",
35	  // Where OPERATIONAL / report notifications go (node-capacity alerts and other
36	  // ops-facing digests). Kept separate from `support_email` so these don't clutter
37	  // the human support inbox — see `reportsEmail()`. Blank falls back to this default,

48	  social_twitter: "",
49	  social_github: "",
50	  social_discord: "",
51	  social_linkedin: "",
52	  social_facebook: "",
53	  social_instagram: "",
54	  social_youtube: "",
55	  footer_text: "",
56	  // Raw provider <script> body injected by components/marketing/LiveChat.tsx.

62	  // below when set. Off by default; needs an API key to actually call Claude.

67	  kb_bot_api_key: "",

85	  kb_bot_daily_cap: "1000",

137	  google_ads_vps_label: "",
138	  google_ads_hosting_label: "",
139	  google_ads_game_label: "",
140	  google_ads_email_label: "",
141	  google_ads_card_label: "",
142	  meta_capi_token: "",
143	  meta_test_event_code: "",

541	
542	/** True-ish coercion for values stored as "true"/"false"/"on"/"1". */
543	export function isTrue(v: string | undefined | null): boolean {
544	  return v === "true" || v === "on" || v === "1";
545	}
546	
547	/** Read one setting, falling back to an explicit default then SETTINGS_DEFAULTS. */
548	export async function getSetting(key: SettingKey | string, fallback?: string): Promise<string> {
549	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
550	  if (row) return row.value;
551	  return fallback ?? SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey] ?? "";
552	}
553	
554	/** Read one setting as a boolean. */
555	export async function getSettingBool(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = false): Promise<boolean> {
556	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
557	  if (row) return isTrue(row.value);
558	  const def = SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey];
559	  return def !== undefined ? isTrue(def) : fallback;
560	}
561	
562	/** Read one setting as an integer (cents, days, counts…). */
563	export async function getSettingInt(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = 0): Promise<number> {
564	  const raw = await getSetting(key, String(fallback));
565	  const n = Number(raw);
566	  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : fallback;
567	}
568	
569	/** Upsert one setting. */
570	export async function setSetting(key: SettingKey | string, value: string): Promise<void> {
571	  await db.setting.upsert({
572	    where: { key },
573	    update: { value },
574	    create: { key, value },
575	  });
576	}
577	
578	/**
579	 * Every setting, with defaults merged under any stored overrides. Secret values
580	 * ARE included — callers that hand this to the client (the settings page) must
581	 * strip SECRET_KEYS themselves.
582	 */
583	export async function getAllSettings(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
584	  const rows = await db.setting.findMany();
585	  const merged: Record<string, string> = { ...SETTINGS_DEFAULTS };
586	  for (const r of rows) merged[r.key] = r.value;
587	  return merged;
588	}
589	
590	/**
591	 * The admin-configured default billing term, in MONTHS, guaranteed to be a term the
592	 * platform can actually sell.
593	 *
594	 * The guarantee is the point. `default_term` was previously the enum
595	 * "monthly"|"quarterly"|"annual" and the platform's real terms are 1/12/24/36 months
596	 * (`VPS_TERMS`) — "quarterly" mapped to nothing at all. Anything stored that
597	 * `VPS_TERMS` does not contain (a legacy row, or a hand-crafted POST that slipped past
598	 * the panel's enum check) falls back to the first term rather than pre-selecting a
599	 * commitment no charge path can price. A wizard that pre-selects an unsellable term
600	 * would fail at `vpsTerm()`'s own silent `?? VPS_TERMS[0]` fallback, charging monthly
601	 * while the review step displayed something else.
602	 */
603	export async function defaultTermMonths(): Promise<number> {
604	  const months = Number(await getSetting("default_term"));
605	  return VPS_TERMS.some((t) => t.months === months) ? months : VPS_TERMS[0].months;
606	}
607	
608	/**
609	 * The public support address, guaranteed non-empty.
610	 *
611	 * Shared rather than inlined because it is rendered into `mailto:` hrefs on the public
612	 * contact page. `saveSettings` happily stores a blank string when an operator clears the
613	 * field, and `mailto:` with no recipient opens an empty compose window — a visitor who
614	 * clicks "Email our team" would be left with nowhere to send it and no error to explain
615	 * why. The hardcoded default is the address the marketing site has always published.
616	 */
617	export async function supportEmail(): Promise<string> {
618	  const v = (await getSetting("support_email")).trim();
619	  return v || SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.support_email;
620	}
621	
622	/**
623	 * The operational / report address, guaranteed non-empty.
624	 *
625	 * Ops-facing notifications (node-capacity WARN/CRITICAL/cleared alerts and similar
626	 * automated reports) route here instead of `supportEmail()` so they don't bury real
627	 * customer mail in the support inbox. Configurable via the `reports_email` setting;
628	 * a blank value falls back to the default reports address (never to support_email).
629	 */
630	export async function reportsEmail(): Promise<string> {
631	  const v = (await getSetting("reports_email")).trim();
632	  return v || SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.reports_email;
633	}

## 2. `lib/discord-bridge.ts` (314 lines, full file read)

**Shape**: one plain GUILD_TEXT channel per ticket/chat conversation in a single private guild — not a thread, not a forum (doc comment 12-24 explains forum channels can't have private threads, and it's moot since the whole guild is private).

**Channel creation + naming:**
- `ensureTicketChannel()` (111-135, private): if `ticket.discordThreadId` exists, reuse it; else `createGuildTextChannel(\`ticket-${ticket.id.slice(-8)}\`, \`Ticket ${ticket.id}: ${ticket.subject}\`)`, posts an opening context message (🎫 subject/priority/customer/admin-link), then `db.ticket.update({ data: { discordThreadId: channelId } as any })`.
